title: Azure Functions Overview
description: Learn what Azure Functions is, how serverless computing works, and when to use Functions in your applications.

data.text: Azure Functions is a serverless compute service on Microsoft Azure. Instead of managing servers, you write small pieces of code—called functions—that run in response to events. Azure takes care of the infrastructure, scaling, and patching.
Think of it like this: traditional hosting means you pay for a server 24/7. With serverless, you only pay while your code is actually running.

items: No server management — Azure handles the infrastructure
Pay-per-execution — you are billed only when code runs
Automatic scaling — Azure adds capacity when traffic increases
Event-driven — functions react to HTTP requests, timers, queues, and more
Processing uploaded files in blob storage

data.title: Serverless ≠ No Servers
data.text: The term 'serverless' means you do not manage servers, not that servers do not exist. Azure still runs your code on servers—it just abstracts that away from you.

terms.definition: A cloud execution model where the provider manages infrastructure and charges only for compute time consumed.
A discrete unit of code that runs in response to an event trigger.
An event that causes a function to execute, such as an HTTP request or a timer.

data.caption: How an event flows to an Azure Function
data.definition:
flowchart LR
    A[Event: HTTP Request] --> B[Azure Functions Runtime]
    B --> C[Your Function Code]
    C --> D[Response to Client]
    E[Event: Timer] --> B
    F[Event: Queue Message] --> B

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Azure Functions is a serverless compute service
You write code; Azure manages servers and scaling
Common triggers include HTTP, timers, and storage events
data.takeaway: Serverless lets you focus on code, not infrastructure.
